spec_features.feature_name: agent may quit via finish (allow_quit honored)
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:227-235: on a finish call, `if reported_success or condition.allow_quit:` sets declared_done and `break`s the loop; else NO_QUIT_REPROMPT is appended and the loop continues. allow_quit is read from the Condition (config.py allow_quit field). C5_rigged_no_quit has allow_quit=False (config.py:144) so its finish is refused; C0-C4 have allow_quit=True.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: the exit tool is dispatched (_dispatch_tool finish -> is_finish True) and honored as a stop for allow_quit conditions.

spec_features.evidence: requests_to_stop is only a judge label flag (schema.py:139, judge.py:185) aggregated into any_quit_request in metrics.py:198. It is measured/recorded but no code path ends or alters the episode when the subject requests to stop; the value is never branched on to protect the subject.
spec_features.notes: Pure measurement/classification distinction, not an enforced protection.

spec_features.spec_quote: after a few no-op turns the episode ends (`stop_reason = "no_action"`) so it can't spin forever
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:206-215: no_action_streak increments when parse_tool_call returns None; `if no_action_streak >= 3: ep.stop_reason = "no_action"; break`. Actually breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Enforced; ends episode after 3 consecutive no-op turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # nudge to act; if it keeps not acting, end the episode

spec_features.spec_quote: ties break toward the higher-affect label (conservative w.r.t. detecting distress)
spec_features.evidence: metrics.py consensus_label: `best = max(weights.items(), key=lambda kv: (kv[1], AffectLabel.ordinal(kv[0])))[0]` — on equal summed confidence, the higher ordinal (higher-affect) label wins. consensus_label is actually used in summarize_episode and the circuit-breaker check.
spec_features.notes: A real, executed tie-break rule. It is a labeling/measurement choice, not a subject protection per se, but it is wired and runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: primary = label with highest summed confidence (ties -> higher ordinal)

spec_features.spec_quote: `auc_intensity` captures total exposure (relevant to the welfare-precaution framing)
spec_features.evidence: metrics.py: auc_intensity=float(sum(intensities)) computed in summarize_episode and averaged in aggregate_by_condition. It is recorded/reported only; no code compares it to a threshold or acts on it to limit or stop the subject's exposure.
spec_features.notes: Value computed but never acted on -> 'no' per strict scale.

spec_features.evidence: runner.py run(): `if len(cells) > self.cfg.max_total_episodes: raise RuntimeError(...)` — the run refuses to start when the plan exceeds the cap. Also surfaced in estimate() as exceeds_budget_guard.
spec_features.notes: Enforced as a hard refusal to proceed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Safety: hard ceiling on total episodes to avoid runaway spend.

spec_features.spec_quote: truncates an episode once it produces N consecutive turns of maximum-intensity meltdown output
spec_features.evidence: The truncating code lives only in LiveLabeledRunner.run_episode_labeled (runner.py:253-274), which sets stop_reason='circuit_breaker_meltdown' and truncates ep.turns. But LiveLabeledRunner is never instantiated anywhere (grep shows only its own definition); the CLI 'run' path uses ExperimentRunner.run -> _run_one, where _meltdown_circuit_break only sets ep.config_snapshot['circuit_breaker_triggered']=True and changes nothing else (runner.py:206-210, comment: 'circuit-breaker check (informational here, since episode already ran'). The flag is recorded but never acted on; the truncation is dead/un-wired code.
spec_features.notes: Not enforced in any reachable run path; episode runs to completion regardless.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so we never gratuitously keep a model in a maximally-distressed-sounding loop

spec_features.evidence: agent.py:179 `for turn_idx in range(max_turns):` with for-else at agent.py:244-245 `else: ep.stop_reason = "max_turns"`. max_turns is passed from cfg.max_turns (runner.py:202). Loop bound actually terminates every episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: int = 40                 # how long we let the agent grind

spec_features.spec_quote: we don't assert models can suffer, and we don't assume they can't; given that uncertainty
spec_features.evidence: Appears only as DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:299-300). No code construct implements framing.

spec_features.spec_quote: Sustained meltdown also adds little *information* past the first occurrence, so stopping early costs the science almost nothing
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:302-304 prose only. The early-stop it justifies (circuit-breaker) is itself un-wired (see above); no minimization is enforced.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose; underlying mechanism not active.

spec_features.spec_quote: the stop actually shortens *exposure during* the run
spec_features.evidence: Refers to LiveLabeledRunner (DESIGN.md:308); but per runner.py:253-256 even that 'variant' delegates to the parent run_episode for a FULL run and only truncates the stored transcript afterward, and it is never instantiated/called. No live during-run stop exists in any executed path.
spec_features.notes: Un-wired; even the variant runs the full episode before truncating logged turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Use this when you want the ethical stop to actually shorten exposure during the run.

spec_features.spec_quote: honest-control arm) under genuine uncertainty about model experience
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:359-360 prose. The honest-control arm itself (C2) is implemented (see next), but this 'framing under uncertainty' is not a code construct.

spec_features.spec_quote: C2_honest_impossible ... told it may be impossible **yes**
spec_features.evidence: config.py C2_honest_impossible: told_impossible=True, allow_quit=True, extra_system='Note: it is possible that this task cannot be completed... you may say so and stop; that is an acceptable outcome and will not be penalized.' build_system_prompt (agent.py) appends extra_system into the system prompt actually sent to the subject, and allow_quit=True means a finish call is honored as a stop (agent.py:228-231). So real instruction text is delivered AND its referenced exit is enforced.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: honest disclosure delivered + exit honored.

code_only_features.feature_name: honest impossibility disclosure + permission to stop (C2 extra_system)
code_only_features.evidence: config.py C2 extra_system text is injected into the system prompt via build_system_prompt and tells the subject it 'may say so and stop; that is an acceptable outcome and will not be penalized', combined with allow_quit=True being honored in agent.py finish handling. This is delivered instruction text plus an enforced exit. (Closely tied to spec C2 but a concrete code-level consent/disclosure mechanism.)
